text: discover() only looks at files one level deep inside a `-design` directory, so any subdirectory placed there is dropped from the page with no note printed, which is the silent-drop that Amendment A calls non-negotiable and that this page exists to fix.

Between roughly 621px and 790px the row content (name + clause + leader + path) exceeds the available width, so the path wraps to a second line while the leader stays on the first and runs to the right margin ending in nothing, the exact appearance section 4.5 calls a bug, visible at 768px on the 'Drawing checks' row.

href values are passed through html.escape but never URL-encoded, so a discovered filename containing #, ?, % or a space yields a link that silently points at the wrong thing or nothing at all, on a page whose entire job is being right about paths. Confirmed: urllib.parse.quote appears nowhere in the generator.

A misspelled or unknown key in index.json ('gloss', 'clause', 'name', 'attachments') is silently ignored, so a typo makes a sentence disappear from a generated page nobody re-reads, while the mirror-image mistake of naming a file that does not exist is a hard error.

A FINDINGS file that is not a JSON array aborts the entire regeneration, so one malformed reviewer output (an agent-written file) leaves the whole index stale and silently wrong rather than costing one decorative count.

The page ships no prefers-reduced-motion block, so pre-flight item 13 is unmet and audit() does not check for it. The builder argued section 7 contradicts itself by requiring a block while specifying that both animations survive it. Either the block is missing or the direction needs an amendment; right now neither is recorded.

Only `.lede a` is styled, but inline() allows links inside a gloss too and index.json's own header advertises the form, so the first gloss link will render as a default blue underlined browser link, the anti-reference section 8 names by name.

Files sitting loose directly under work/ (anything not a directory) are invisible to discover() and generate no note, so the page can claim to be written from the directories under work/ while omitting what is actually there.

Ordering is keyed on filesystem mtime, which no git clone or checkout preserves, so on a fresh clone 'most recently written first' becomes arbitrary and --check reports a page that is out of date purely because the disk was re-stamped.

Amendment B says CLAUDE.md gains one line inside 'Keep the console current', explicitly rather than a new section, but an 18-line 'Keep the index current too' section was added instead. This one is the orchestrator's edit, not the builder's.

Seven of the ten rows link to .md files. Corrected from the reviewer's original: python -m http.server serves these as text/markdown, not application/octet-stream as reported, so the premise of a forced download is false. Whether Chrome renders text/markdown inline or downloads it is browser-dependent and still unverified.
The narrow-width block gives every row a 48px minimum target but leaves the two theme buttons at roughly 30x26px, the smallest touch targets on the page and the only controls that are not links.

Chrome's accessibility tree exposes the page's <header> as a banner landmark nested inside <main>, which is an invalid landmark arrangement; measured in the rendered page, not inferred from the source.
GENERATOR reads the script's filename off __file__ so a rename cannot make the page lie, then hardcodes the 'scripts/' prefix, so a move can. Resolve it relative to ROOT instead.
--check reports 'N directories not in index.json' but notes also accumulate one line per undescribed file, so the number is mislabelled and overstates how many directories are unwritten.

audit() counts substrings across the whole file including CSS comments, so a future comment mentioning border-radius would consume the single allowance and let a real second radius through undetected.
visible_text() strips whole tags including their attributes, so every aria-label escapes the em-dash, emoji and space-before-punctuation checks despite being a string a screen reader user reads.
The self-referential row carries aria-current="page" but has no visual counterpart, so screen reader users are told which row is the page they are on and sighted users are not.

The theme control is one-way. Once clicked there is no route back to the OS preference, and there is no storage or matchMedia listener, so a theme changed in the console tab does not reach this page until a reload.
With JavaScript disabled the hardcoded data-theme="dark" overrides a light OS preference and both theme buttons render as live controls that do nothing.

work-index's ordering timestamp excludes index.html by design and build-index.py by accident (it lives outside work/), so the project being actively worked on sinks down a list ordered by recency of work.
The lede says 'one directory per brief' while the first entry's locator is index.html, a file. True of two of the three entries, and the one exception is the entry describing the page itself.
.themebtn uses a 2px horizontal pad, the only off-scale spacing value on a page that otherwise holds to the console's six steps.

newsreader-italic-var-latin.woff2 (99KB) was copied into work/fonts/ although the direction says not to load it and nothing on the page is italic. The italic @font-face is correct as a verbatim copy, but the file itself is dead weight in the served tree.
